landscape.label: 2026 Price Guide
title: Water Heater
Installation Cost
landscape.speak: How much does it cost to install a new water heater in Iowa City in 2026? Most installs run from about nine hundred fifty dollars to six thousand dollars. Here's what each type of system costs, and what moves your price.
landscape.say: How much does it cost to install a new water heater in Iowa City in 2026? Most installs run from about $950 to $6,000. Here's what each type of system costs, and what moves your price.

landscape.label: Cost by System Type
landscape.title: Total installed cost by system
landscape.speak: Here's the average total installed cost by system in 2026. An electric tankless heater runs about eleven hundred dollars to twenty-seven hundred dollars. An electric tank, twelve hundred dollars to three thousand dollars. A gas tank, thirteen hundred dollars to four thousand fifty dollars. A heat pump or hybrid, two thousand dollars to sixty-three hundred dollars. And a gas tankless system, thirty-three hundred dollars to six thousand two hundred fifty dollars.
landscape.say: Here's the average total installed cost by system in 2026. An electric tankless heater runs about $1,100 to $2,700. An electric tank, $1,200 to $3,000. A gas tank, $1,300 to $4,050. A heat pump or hybrid, $2,000 to $6,300. And a gas tankless system, $3,300 to $6,250.

landscape.label: Unit vs. Labor
landscape.title: Where the money goes
landscape.speak: Where does the money go? The unit itself runs about seven hundred dollars to forty-eight hundred dollars and labor runs three hundred dollars to thirty-five hundred dollars. Gas tankless costs the most to install, because it usually needs a bigger gas line and different venting.
landscape.say: Where does the money go? The unit itself runs about $700 to $4,800, and labor runs $300 to $3,500. Gas tankless costs the most to install, because it usually needs a bigger gas line and different venting.

landscape.label: Tank or Tankless?
landscape.title: Tank or tankless?

rows.label: Hot water
rows.a: Limited to what's in the tank
rows.b: Continuous while a tap is open

rows.label: Install work
rows.b: Often needs gas line & venting changes

landscape.say: Tank or tankless? A tank keeps a set amount of water hot and ready, costs less upfront, and is usually a straight swap. A tankless heater heats water only when a tap is open and mounts on the wall, but costs more, because it often needs gas line and venting changes. Busy households that keep running out of hot water often do better with tankless.

landscape.say: What moves your price? The type and size of the unit, whether the gas line needs to be upsized, venting changes, and a tight utility space, where a wall-mounted tankless unit often fits when a new tank won't.

landscape.label: Time to Replace?
landscape.title: Signs it's time to replace
items: A leak is an emergency: call now
landscape.note: Most tank water heaters last about 8 to 12 years.
landscape.say: When is it time to replace? Most tank heaters last about 8 to 12 years. Watch for water leaking from the bottom, rusty or discolored hot water, popping or rumbling sounds, or hot water that runs out faster than it used to. A tank over 10 years old showing any of these is worth replacing. And a leaking tank is an emergency.

landscape.label: Iowa Hard Water Tip
landscape.title: Eastern Iowa hard water tip

tiles.s: Now and then, to slow the buildup
Scale collects in the heat exchanger

landscape.note: Ask your gas or electric utility about rebates on efficient models.
landscape.say: One local tip: Eastern Iowa water is hard. Minerals settle in the tank as scale, which makes the heater work harder. Flushing the tank now and then slows the buildup, and tankless units need periodic descaling. And ask your utility about rebates on efficient models.
